newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish police suspect Germans aiding ETA - papers.
newsitem.headline: Spanish police suspect Germans aiding ETA - papers.

text.p: Spanish authorities suspect Germans were among four people linked to the Basque guerrilla group ETA who fled a Madrid safe house packed with weapons at the weekend, newspapers said on Sunday.
Police were searching for two men and two women on Sunday, a day after discovering the arsenal along with newspaper clippings of prominent Spaniards and maps of Madrid in a small flat.

An accidental explosion inside the flat early on Saturday aroused neighbours' suspicions. The four fled the apartment complex hurriedly after a neighbour knocked on their door to inquire and said he was going to alert police.
Police arrived minutes later and found 100 kg (220 lbs) of the explosive ammonal, TNT, grenade launchers, assault rifles, a revolver and bomb-making components inside.
The daily El Pais said the flat had been rented in February by a woman who used German documents and the doorbell listed two German names.
The daily El Mundo said two of the four residents used German documentation and, according to neighbours, had a foreign accent and appearance.

Spanish authorities have asked Interpol to check with German police on the authenticity of the German identity documents, the papers said. Interior inistry and police officials could not be reached for comment.
ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, has killed about 800 people in a 29-year campaign for an independent state in parts of northern Spain and southern France.
Authorities said they suspect the safe house was used by ETA's "Commando Madrid", a cell believed to be behind past attacks in the capital.
El Pais quoted police investigators as saying they were certain a foreigner was active in Commando Madrid.
The paper said the Interior Ministry has been investigating the possible collaboration of German nationals with ETA for some months.
The investigation began after the arrest in France of a German woman detained in November 1996 with Juan Luis Aguirre "Isuntza" Lete, a senior ETA figure.
